No discrete central-memory (Tcm) cluster was resolved. CCR7 was not included in the TotalSeq-C panel, so Tcm cells cannot be gated on surface CCR7 in this dataset; scoring the transcriptional profile instead (CCR7, SELL and CD27 detected with surface CD45RA low) identifies 450 of 18,843 CD8 cells (2.4%), distributed across 9 clusters with no cluster exceeding 7.2% Tcm-profile cells (Supplementary Table S3). Central-memory cells are therefore present as a minor transcriptional profile within the naive and effector-memory compartments rather than as a separable population, consistent with the predominantly naive composition of the infant CD8 compartment.

Because the five longitudinally sampled participants were not selected at random but by sample availability, the cohort cannot support population-level inference; the longitudinal claims are within-participant trajectories in which each participant serves as their own baseline, which limits but does not eliminate the effect of that selection. CMV co-infection is a further confound we cannot fully separate: CMV-annotated clonotypes were detected in all five participants, CMV drives effector differentiation, and CMV serostatus was not measured directly in this cohort, so any comparison of infant and adult effector phenotypes may partly reflect differences in CMV exposure rather than age or HIV status.

Of 12,758 unique CD8 clonotypes, 834 were expanded beyond a single cell. Clonotypes of exactly two cells account for 304 of these (36.5% of expanded clonotypes) but only 608 cells (11.3% of all cells in expanded clonotypes), so in the cell-weighted analyses reported here they contribute a minority of the signal (Supplementary Figure S2E).
